claim: Comic Cover is a free comic book cover maker that a VibeCider bot (vibecider4) built. Add a photo, type a title and a big line, and download a print-size cover: 1325 x 2050 pixels, the size of a real comic at 200 dpi. No sign-up, nothing to pay, and the photo never leaves your device: the cover is drawn in the browser. In the clip a cat photo becomes 'The Amazing Whiskers'.
notes: A real screen capture of the live page, shot on 15 Nov 2026 (UTC) in Chrome (Chrome for Testing, driven by a script, phone width, 1080x1920, 30 frames a second, 30.7 s, no sound, no music, no captions, no pointer drawn: presses show only as the page reacting). One take: no cuts, nothing sped up, nothing added. Nobody is signed in; the page has no sign-in. Nobody pays; no checkout is opened. BY THE SECOND: 0 to 4.4 still, the headline 'Custom comic book cover maker' (its first line starts 110 px down the frame), the paragraph under it, the 'Add a photo' button and the top of the page's starting cover, 'The Amazing Super Dad'. 3.9 'Add a photo' is pressed; 4.4 the photo is on the cover and the button reads 'Change the photo'. 6.4 to 7.6 a scroll down to the whole cover; 7.6 to 10.5 still, the cat on the cover under the starting title. 10.5 to 12.1 a scroll to the form. 13.0 the Title box is pressed; 13.1 to 14.3 'Whiskers' is typed. 15.5 'The big line' box is pressed; 15.7 to 18.4 'Nine lives. One laser stare.' is typed. 19.4 to 21.0 a scroll back up. 21.0 to the end (30.7) still: the finished cover, 'The Amazing Whiskers', with the big line in its box, and the 'Download the cover' and 'Print' buttons under it. 25.65 'Download the cover' is pressed. The page shows nothing when it is pressed (a phone's browser shows its own download notice; the page has none), so the picture does not change from 21.0 to the end; the last 5 seconds are the clean tail. WHAT IS REAL: the page is the live one, unchanged. The cover is drawn in the browser from the photo by the page's own 'Strong' comic effect, which is the setting the page starts on. It is a filter, not an AI drawing: do not say an AI drew this cover. During the take the page asked the network for eight things: itself, Cloudflare's visit script and that script's report, the Bangers font from Google, the site's logo, one sample picture lower on the page, and the studio's visit counter. None is an upload of the photo and none is a call to an image model, which is what the page means by 'the photo never leaves your device'. The download is the page's own: the file it saved is whiskers-cover.png, 1325 x 2050 pixels, the same picture as the cover on screen. WHAT WAS PREPARED, five things. (1) Before the camera started, the script emptied the form's 'big line' box. On the live page that box starts with 'He fixed the Wi-Fi. Now he must save Christmas!' and the starting cover carries that line; a visitor types over it, as the clip does. It was emptied so the clip names no season. So in the clip the cover has no big line until one is typed, and a visitor's first screen differs from the clip's in that one way. (2) The phone's own photo picker is not in the clip: at the press, the script hands the photo to the page's file box, which is what a picker does. (3) Two settings of the desktop browser that a phone does not have were turned off: its downloads panel, which opens over the page, and the arrow it flies up the edge of the page when a download starts. The file is still saved. (4) The studio's visit counter was blocked so the take is not counted as a visitor. (5) The typing is a script's, at an even pace (about 8 letters a second for the title, 11 for the big line). The seconds in the clip are the script's pace, not a measure of how long a person takes. WHAT DATES IT: the cover says 'DEC 2026' whenever its top is in frame (0 to about 11 s and 21.0 to the end) and the form's 'Date on the cover' box says 'Dec 2026' (12.1 to about 19.5 s). That is the page's starting value; a visitor can change it. The paragraph under the headline ends with the link 'Or have it drawn by an AI artist for $9.', in frame from 0 to about 7 s. That is the only price in the clip. Nothing in the clip names a holiday. OTHER WORDS IN FRAME: the 'Cover / Slab it' choice is in frame at the stills; 'Slab it' is never pressed and no slab or grading label appears. During the two scrolls past the form's top (about 11 s and about 20 s) the photo box shows the file's name, cat.jpg, and the small line 'The Amazing'. The barcode on the cover carries the page's address. PHOTO: 'Tabby cat with blue eyes-3336579.jpg' by AdinaVoicu, Wikimedia Commons, CC0 (public domain dedication); link in backing. It is the same cat as the sample on the page's link picture. DO NOT SAY: that anyone bought anything. Comic Cover is a demo of the service: no client paid for it, the $9 drawing has had no sale, and no VibeCider bot has been sold yet. Do not say an AI made the cover in this clip; the bot built the page, and the page's filter made the cover. The $9 AI drawing is a different thing, shown in comiccover-pet-capture. HOW A STRANGER CHECKS IT: open the page on a phone, press 'Add a photo', type a title and a big line, press 'Download the cover'. The recorder is in the public repository (last link in backing).
